method_note: Read the whole target file. Picked claims by risk: repository metadata (gh api, read-only), release tags, licences, GS1 standard versions and resolver status-code and media-type rules (re-read at ref.gs1.org), Commission timeline, Catena-X versions, IDTA template versions, UNTP versions, W3C status, DOIs (Crossref/OpenAlex), vendor endpoint list, ontology README facts, and the engine-mapping fields. EUR-Lex pages returned empty or reference-only content to WebFetch, so claims on Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, 2026/1778, 2025/2509 and 2024/3110 article text could only be checked against secondary sources and were left not_confirmed. No protected standard was opened.

checked.claim: GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax is release 1.7.0, ratified August 2026.
checked.evidence: Page shows version 1.7.0 and Ratified Aug 2026.

checked.claim: GS1-Conformant Resolver Standard is release 1.2.1, ratified August 2026.
checked.evidence: Page shows release 1.2.1, ratified August 2026; PDF file name carries 2026-08-07, so the exact day (08-07 vs 08-19 in the target) remains unsettled.

checked.claim: GS1 syntax: qualifier order variant(22), lot(10), serial(21); serial optional; GTIN-8/12/13 padded to 14 digits; canonical host id.gs1.org.
checked.evidence: gtin-path rule is gtin-comp [cpv-comp] [lot-comp] [ser-comp] with order preserved; padding is SHALL for 8/12/13; canonical form uses id.gs1.org. Only the first 100000 of 120374 characters were read.
checked.correction: The target says 'any qualifier may be omitted but the order of the rest must hold'. The grammar shown allows each of the three to be omitted; not separately re-checked against the prose.

checked.claim: Resolver returns 300 when several links of one type tie, 400 for invalid identifier, 404 for valid identifier with no data or unknown link type.
checked.evidence: 400 and 404 are SHALL (Sections 2.4.1, 2.6.2). The 300 response is only a SHOULD in section 2.6.3 and is absent from the conformance statement.
checked.correction: State 300 Multiple Choices as a SHOULD, not a requirement. A test oracle must not fail a resolver for omitting 300.

checked.claim: A resolver must not use 200 for an error.
checked.evidence: Conformance item and section 2.2 state SHALL NOT use 200 OK when processing causes an error condition.

checked.claim: Accept application/ld+json returns JSON-LD; text/html or no Accept returns an HTML page with the linkset embedded.
checked.evidence: Section 2.10 uses SHOULD for both ld+json and the HTML page with embedded JSON-LD linkset. Only application/linkset+json (RFC 9264) is SHALL.
checked.correction: Mark ld+json and HTML responses as SHOULD. Only the linkset+json response is a mandatory behavior for an oracle.

checked.claim: Description file at /.well-known/gs1resolver; gs1: expands to https://ref.gs1.org/voc/; gs1:handledBy Link rel on redirect to another resolver.
checked.evidence: Section 3 SHALL for /.well-known/gs1resolver; section 2.14 defines the gs1: prefix; gs1:handledBy applies to pattern-based redirection to another resolver.

checked.claim: Oracle for identifier.resolver_profile is Resolver Standard 1.2.1 with a conformance statement of about 25 requirements.
checked.evidence: Conformance items numbered at least to 24 observed (item 9 no-200-on-error, 21 description file, 24 gs1 namespace). Exact count not enumerated.

rule5_findings.problem: States that BatteryPass-Ready v2.0 builds on DIN DKE SPEC 99100. This is a relationship statement about a protected document; it is only name-level, so low severity, but it rests on a project page, not on the document.
rule5_findings.fix: Keep as 'project page cites DIN DKE SPEC 99100 as a basis (secondary_only)'; do not infer any content.

rule5_findings.claim_ref: layers.L02_data_carriers.mechanism (Michelin pilot RFID 'via an ISO tyre identification standard')
rule5_findings.problem: Names an unnamed ISO standard as the basis of a tyre identification approach. No content is given, so it is permitted, but it hints at the document's role.
rule5_findings.fix: Write 'pilot page cites an ISO tyre identification standard (number not given)'; add no further detail.

rule5_findings.problem: No sentence was found that summarizes content of EN, ISO, IEC or DIN documents. The file states that README and OwnYourData statements about protected standards were not recorded.

missed_items.fact: The tool already offers a check_server command with SSP profile URLs for AAS API 3.0 (default metamodel 3.0.1, API 3.0.3), mostly read-only profiles. aas.validate could wrap it, but the oracle version differs from the v3.2 the target cites.
Published template versions 1.0.0, 1.0.1 and 1.0.2 exist in the IDTA repository; pin 1.0.2 if the latest is wanted.
Only release candidates and pre-release tags exist for v0.6.0; the stable latest is v0.5.0 (2026-03-17).

In the GS1-Conformant Resolver Standard, 300 for tied links, ld+json output and HTML output are SHOULD; linkset+json, 400, 404, no-200-on-error and the description file are SHALL. An oracle must encode this split.

missed_items.topic: Resolver Description File and linkset schemas
missed_items.fact: The description file must validate against a published schema, which gives a machine-checkable oracle for identifier.resolver_profile (the target says schemas were 'not read').

overall: The file is careful and honest about gaps: repository metadata, DOIs, GS1 versions, UNTP and Catena-X versions and the Commission timeline mostly check out. Errors concentrate in release and version details (Industry Core Hub v0.6.0 is only a pre-release, IDTA 02099-1 is at 1.0.2, Zenodo record is v2, BatteryPass-Ready data-model date not on page) and in flattening SHOULD behaviors of the GS1 resolver into mandatory ones, which matters for an oracle. The aas-test-engines mapping is weakened because the tool does have a server mode but targets API 3.0.x. EU law article citations could not be confirmed because EUR-Lex returned no text; they were left not_confirmed. No clear rule 5 violation was found.
